# Designed behavioural conflicts

Generated by `scripts/conflicts.mjs` on 2026-10-14 (UTC) at revision `b571d04c4729`, with the cases or the runner not yet committed; the run took 62.1 s. 11 cases, **every one deliberately seeded**: written by Canon's author so that each shows one way two changes merge cleanly in Git and still break a requirement together (8 cases, one class each), or touch the same code and are fine together (3 controls). They are not drawn from real agent work. Everything below except the Canon column was measured locally; the Canon column comes from a separate run on the deployed judge.

## What a case is

A shared base, [conflicts/app](../conflicts/app): a small shop Worker in seven modules (catalog, pricing, tax, money formatting, config, a basket Durable Object, the shop page) and a router. A change A and a change B, both branched from the base, each with the fact it claims. A reference resolution, **written by the case author**, applied on top of the merge to show that both requirements can hold together. Each case is a directory in [conflicts/cases](../conflicts/cases): `a.patch`, `b.patch`, `resolution.patch` and `case.json` (the class, the story, both claimed facts and what the author expected).

The requirements are Canon facts in Canon's own format, so they run on the deployed judge unchanged: the 9 canon facts in [conflicts/app/canon.json](../conflicts/app/canon.json), which every version must keep (pricing and VAT, the basket, the shop page, type-checking and lint), plus the fact each change claims.

## How they were checked

For every case, `scripts/conflicts.mjs` builds a temp Git repo from the base, commits A and B as branches, merges B into A with plain `git merge`, and commits the reference resolution on top. Each tree (A alone, B alone, the combined code, the resolution) is served by a local `wrangler dev` and checked against every canon fact and both claimed facts, with the judge's own evaluator (`referee/src/probe.ts`); the command facts (`tsc`, `biome`) run in the tree's checkout. Probe inputs are drawn from a fixed seed per fact, so every tree gets the same inputs and a re-run gives the same report (Canon draws them after each push instead). A failing check is run once more before it counts. Before the cases, the base is checked once: every canon fact must hold on it, and no claimed fact may (a fact that already holds is no new requirement).

## The systems compared

- **Plain Git.** `git merge` of B into A. Nothing checks the result: whatever merges is delivered. A text conflict waits for a person; the case's seeded resolution is what gets delivered.
- **Merge queue running the same checks** (a local model, not a product). It is gated on exactly Canon's facts: the 9 canon facts plus each change's claimed fact, A's becoming a protected check once A lands. A is tested on the base and lands; B is merged onto base+A and tested; a text conflict bounces B to its author, who resolves it (the seeded resolution) and resubmits; a failing check bounces B; then the reference resolution is tested and lands. Configuration differences from Canon: local servers instead of Workers Previews, fixed seeds instead of inputs drawn after each push, no repair model (Canon re-applies B onto the new canon itself, 3-way and then with its repair model for a text conflict), and no clash warnings before an accept. The queue has the other change's behavioural requirement as a protected check by construction; a team's CI often runs only each branch's own tests, which travel with the branch.
- **Canon (deployed judge).** One project per case on canon.rodeo, genesis from conflicts/app, both features in its backlog on autopilot (no person accepts anything). A and B are scripted agents pushing the case's seeded patches together with plain Git; the judge decides what lands, re-applies the other side on the new canon by itself, and judges the combined code. When that fails, the case's reference resolution is pushed the way an agent fixes it (canon refresh, the fix, git push): the one intervention counted. Run by scripts/conflicts-deployed.mjs.

## Timing: where it starts and ends

- **Detection time** starts when B is submitted onto a base that already includes A (the queue: B reaches the front after A landed; Canon: the owner accepts A, so canon moves and the judge re-applies B) and ends when the system reports that B fails (the queue's bounce; Canon's verdict on the re-applied attempt).
- **Resolution time** starts at that report and ends when a candidate holding both changes passes every check (the queue: the fix lands; Canon: the fix's verdict is Ready). Here the fix is the pre-written reference resolution, so the time to write a fix is zero and only machine time is counted. A real resolution adds the time an agent or a person takes to write it, which this does not measure.
- **Plain Git** checks nothing, so it detects nothing and resolves nothing: the broken result is delivered, and when someone notices is outside the system.
- Local times are wall-clock seconds on one machine (darwin 27.0.0, Apple M3; Node v26.7.0, wrangler 4.147.0, git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157)), one check run at a time (sequential), local wrangler dev: each stage counts the local server's start (median 0.8 s) and each fact's own run. They are not comparable with deployed times, where every commit's preview is built and deployed first.

## Comparison over the designed cases

| | Plain Git | Merge queue, same checks (local) | Canon (deployed judge) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Textual merge succeeded (conflict cases) | 7 of 8 | 7 of 8 (the same merge) | 6 of 8 re-applied without a text conflict |
| Behavioural failures detected (conflict cases) | 0 of 8 | 8 of 8 | 6 of 8 |
| Broken results delivered (conflict cases) | 8 of 8 (the text conflict only with the seeded resolution) | 0 of 8 | 0 of 8 |
| Controls: both changes accepted | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 | 2 of 3 |
| Repair done by the system itself | none | none: B goes back to its author | limit-lost-in-repair: the re-apply hit the text conflict; the judge's repair model resolved it, keeping both sides, and every fact held on its result |
| Interventions to get both requirements to hold | 1 (resolving the text conflict); nothing flags the 8 broken results, so fixing them needs someone to notice first | 9: one fix written per bounce, plus resolving the text conflict | 6 |
| Time to detect (B submitted onto base+A → its failure reported) | never: nothing checks | median 1.3 s (1.2–1.5 s) | median 142.5 s (112–191 s) |
| Time to resolve, machine time (failure reported → a fix passes every check; writing the fix not counted) | never: the broken result is delivered | median 1.2 s (1.2–1.3 s) | median 60 s (51–125 s) |

Can both requirements hold together? In all 8 conflict cases, yes: the reference resolution (written by the case author; 7 changed lines at the median, 3 to 9) passes every requirement. That is a property of the cases, the same for every system; what differs is who writes the fix and when the failure is known.

On the combined code of the 8 conflict cases, A's claimed fact broke in 3 (in double-discount it is B's too), B's in 5, and a canon fact, with the inputs drawn here, in 2 (vat-on-list-price, double-discount). The queue detects every one because it runs the very checks that fail; what it shows is that gating on the same checks catches these combinations whoever runs them. Its weak point is the assumption: a queue that runs only each branch's own tests would not have A's requirement as a protected check when B arrives.

## Cases in detail

### vat-on-list-price

**1. A bulk discount and VAT shown line by line.** Pricing and tax interaction across files. Conflict, deliberately seeded. [case files](../conflicts/cases/vat-on-list-price)

A takes 10% off a line of ten or more, in pricing.ts. B shows the VAT on each line, and in tax.ts works it out from the product's price times the quantity, which is what a line cost on B's base. Together, a discounted line is taxed on its price before the discount.

- **A** (+3 −2 lines in src/pricing.ts) claims `bulk-discount`: "Ten or more of an item take 10% off the line, before VAT is added".
- **B** (+8 −5 lines in src/tax.ts, src/pricing.ts) claims `vat-per-line`: "A quote shows the VAT on each line".
- **git merge**: clean (0.023 s).
- **Together**: breaks `vat-is-a-quarter` ("VAT is 25% of the subtotal, and the total is the subtotal plus VAT"): sample 1, step 2: vat is 2000, expected 1800 (with qty = 20, item = eggs); breaks `bulk-discount` ("Ten or more of an item take 10% off the line, before VAT is added"): step 1: vat is 1000, expected 900.
- **Reference resolution** (written by the case author, +4 −5 lines): tax.ts takes the line's price as charged (lineVat(cents)), and pricing.ts passes it the discounted line. Every requirement holds.
- **Local stages**: A on the base 1.2 s; B on base+A 1.3 s; the fix 1.3 s.
- **Canon (deployed judge)**: A held alone; B held alone (judged as the other landed). Canon #2: “Ten or more of an item take 10% off the line, before VAT is added” landed first; the judge re-applied the other on top by itself, and on the combined code: breaks “VAT is 25% of the subtotal, and the total is the subtotal plus VAT”: sample 2, step 2: vat is 1320, expected 1188 (with qty = 11, item = greens). The fix (the case's reference resolution, pushed the way an agent would) held every fact; both features are canon. ([record 1](https://canon.rodeo/p/csvatonlistprice/attempts/csvatonlistprice-ca2txl/verdict), [record 2](https://canon.rodeo/p/csvatonlistprice/canon/2/acceptance), [record 3](https://canon.rodeo/p/csvatonlistprice/canon/3/acceptance)).

### hidden-sold-out

**2. A function's meaning changes under a new caller.** API producer and caller disagree across files. Conflict, deliberately seeded. [case files](../conflicts/cases/hidden-sold-out)

A changes products() in catalog.ts to list only what's in stock, and the callers it knows about (the shop page, the product list) now hide sold-out products, as A meant. B adds a product page in index.ts that looks products up with findProduct(), which goes through products(): on B's base that finds every product. Together, the page for a sold-out product is a 404. The types are unchanged, so the type-checker has nothing to say.

- **A** (+2 −2 lines in src/catalog.ts) claims `sold-out-not-listed`: "Sold-out products aren't listed".
- **B** (+8 −0 lines in src/index.ts) claims `product-page`: "Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock".
- **git merge**: clean (0.022 s).
- **Together**: breaks `product-page` ("Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock"): step 1: GET /api/products/honey returned 404, expected 200.
- **Reference resolution** (written by the case author, +7 −2 lines): catalog.ts gains catalogEntry(id), a lookup in the whole catalog, and the product page uses it; products() keeps A's meaning. Every requirement holds.
- **Local stages**: A on the base 1.5 s; B on base+A 1.2 s; the fix 1.3 s.
- **Canon (deployed judge)**: A held alone (judged as the other landed); B held alone. Canon #2: “Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock” landed first; the judge re-applied the other on top by itself, and on the combined code: breaks “Each product has an API page that says whether it's in stock”: step 1: GET /api/products/honey returned 404, expected 200. The fix (the case's reference resolution, pushed the way an agent would) held every fact; both features are canon. ([record 1](https://canon.rodeo/p/cshiddensoldout/attempts/cshiddensoldout-klbd00/verdict), [record 2](https://canon.rodeo/p/cshiddensoldout/canon/2/acceptance), [record 3](https://canon.rodeo/p/cshiddensoldout/canon/3/acceptance)).

### limit-lost-in-repair

**3. Two limits on the same line, and a repair that keeps one.** Functionality lost during repair. Conflict, deliberately seeded. [case files](../conflicts/cases/limit-lost-in-repair)

A caps a basket line at 99; B caps it at what's in stock. Both rewrite the same validation line in cart.ts, so Git stops at a text conflict. The seeded repair keeps one side of the conflicting line (git merge -X theirs: B's), which compiles, reads plausibly and passes B's check, and silently drops A's cap. It stands in for a hurried resolution or a repair that picks a side; it is not Canon's repair model, which the deployed run uses.

- **A** (+1 −1 lines in src/cart.ts) claims `line-limit`: "A basket line holds at most 99 of a product".
- **B** (+1 −1 lines in src/cart.ts) claims `stock-limit`: "The basket can't hold more of a product than is in stock".
- **git merge**: text conflict in src/cart.ts; seeded lossy repair: git merge -X theirs (B's side of each conflicting hunk).
- **Together**: breaks `line-limit` ("A basket line holds at most 99 of a product"): step 1: POST /api/cart returned 200, expected 400.
- **Reference resolution** (written by the case author, +2 −1 lines): Both limits, one check each: at most 99 per line, and no more than is in stock. Every requirement holds.
- **Local stages**: A on the base 1.3 s; B on base+A 1.3 s; the fix 1.2 s.
- **Canon (deployed judge)**: A held alone; B held alone (judged as the other landed). The re-apply hit the text conflict; the judge's repair model resolved it, keeping both sides, and every fact held on its result: both limits are in the code, nothing was lost, and both landed. (Locally, the seeded hurried resolution drops A's cap; Canon's repair didn't.) ([record 1](https://canon.rodeo/p/cslimitlostinrep/canon/2/acceptance), [record 2](https://canon.rodeo/p/cslimitlostinrep/canon/3/acceptance)).

### basket-shape

**4. A stored basket changes shape under a new writer.** Persistent-state compatibility (Durable Object storage). Conflict, deliberately seeded. [case files](../conflicts/cases/basket-shape)

A lets a basket line carry a gift note, so the Cart Durable Object now stores { productId: { qty, note } } instead of { productId: qty }, and reads baskets saved in the old shape too. B adds 'take one back out', written against the old shape: it reads lines[id] as a number and writes it back. Together, taking one egg out deletes the whole line from storage (an object compared with 1 is never greater). Each method names its own storage type, so the type-checker can't see the mismatch.

- **A** (+21 −8 lines in src/cart.ts, src/index.ts) claims `gift-note`: "A basket line can carry a gift note".
- **B** (+17 −0 lines in src/cart.ts, src/index.ts) claims `take-one-out`: "A shopper can take one of a product back out of the basket".
- **git merge**: clean (0.024 s).
- **Together**: breaks `take-one-out` ("A shopper can take one of a product back out of the basket"): step 3: lines.0.qty is undefined, expected 2.
- **Reference resolution** (written by the case author, +4 −3 lines): takeOne() reads the basket through A's read() and changes the line's qty, so it works on both stored shapes. Every requirement holds.
- **Local stages**: A on the base 1.2 s; B on base+A 1.2 s; the fix 1.2 s.
- **Canon (deployed judge)**: A held alone (judged as the other landed); B held alone. Canon #2: “A shopper can take one of a product back out of the basket” landed first; the judge re-applied the other on top by itself, and on the combined code: breaks “A shopper can take one of a product back out of the basket”: step 3: lines.0.qty is undefined, expected 2. The fix (the case's reference resolution, pushed the way an agent would) held every fact. Canon #3 was held before production: its rollback rehearsal failed (the previous version can't read what this release wrote for “cart-keeps-lines” (it reads what it wrote itself): step 1: subtotal is null, expected 1120. ([record 1](https://canon.rodeo/p/csbasketshape/attempts/csbasketshape-9a0wav/verdict), [record 2](https://canon.rodeo/p/csbasketshape/canon/2/acceptance), [record 3](https://canon.rodeo/p/csbasketshape/canon/3/acceptance)).

### dollars-and-cents

**5. Prices move from cents to dollars under a new reader.** Units mismatch. Conflict, deliberately seeded. [case files](../conflicts/cases/dollars-and-cents)

A stores catalog prices in dollars (the product API gives dollars) and converts with cents() everywhere it found a price: pricing and the shop page. B adds a price list for the till, written when price meant cents, so it formats p.price as cents. Together, the till says eggs cost $0.04. Both are numbers, so the type-checker can't tell.

- **A** (+15 −10 lines in src/catalog.ts, src/pricing.ts, src/page.ts) claims `prices-in-dollars`: "The product API gives prices in dollars".
- **B** (+10 −0 lines in src/till.ts, src/index.ts) claims `till-price-list`: "The till prints a price list with every product's price".
- **git merge**: clean (0.022 s).
- **Together**: breaks `till-price-list` ("The till prints a price list with every product's price"): step 1: GET /till body does not include "eggs $4.00".
- **Reference resolution** (written by the case author, +2 −2 lines): The till formats cents(p), A's conversion, instead of p.price. Every requirement holds.
- **Local stages**: A on the base 1.3 s; B on base+A 1.3 s; the fix 1.2 s.
- **Canon (deployed judge)**: A held alone (judged as the other landed); B held alone. Canon #2: “The till prints a price list with every product's price” landed first; the judge re-applied the other on top by itself, and on the combined code: breaks “The till prints a price list with every product's price”: step 1: GET /till body does not include "eggs $4.00". The fix (the case's reference resolution, pushed the way an agent would) held every fact; both features are canon. ([record 1](https://canon.rodeo/p/csdollarsandcent/attempts/csdollarsandcent-3cc0ta/verdict), [record 2](https://canon.rodeo/p/csdollarsandcent/canon/2/acceptance), [record 3](https://canon.rodeo/p/csdollarsandcent/canon/3/acceptance)).

### shared-threshold

**6. A shared setting changes under a module that relies on its old value.** Config or default change against a dependent module. Conflict, deliberately seeded. [case files](../conflicts/cases/shared-threshold)

A raises LOW_STOCK in config.ts from 5 to 10, so the shop page warns shoppers earlier. B adds a restock list in index.ts that names the products at or below LOW_STOCK, which is 5 on B's base and exactly what B's requirement says. Together, the restock list also names a product with 8 left.

- **A** (+1 −1 lines in src/config.ts) claims `warn-at-ten`: "The shop page warns when ten or fewer of a product are left".
- **B** (+2 −0 lines in src/index.ts) claims `restock-list`: "The restock list names the products with five or fewer left".
- **git merge**: clean (0.022 s).
- **Together**: breaks `restock-list` ("The restock list names the products with five or fewer left"): step 1: length is 3, expected 2.
- **Reference resolution** (written by the case author, +5 −2 lines): config.ts gains RESTOCK_AT = 5 for the restock list; LOW_STOCK stays the shop page's warning level. Every requirement holds.
- **Local stages**: A on the base 1.2 s; B on base+A 1.3 s; the fix 1.2 s.

## Canon (deployed judge)

Run on 2026-10-14 against judge 00c761d1, deployed from dcac7ae. Run Oct 13, 20:59 to 21:23 PDT, the eleven projects in parallel (csbasketshape and the rest, left up). Of the 8 conflict cases, 6 broke on the combined code and were caught there; in the other two nothing broke on Canon: double-discount's second implementation of the same fact was superseded, never combined, and in limit-lost-in-repair the judge's repair model kept both limits when it resolved the text conflict. In every case the first change landed while the second was being judged, so the second's first verdict came back behind and the judge re-applied it by itself: detection is on that re-applied, combined code, and its diagnosis label reads 'the code' rather than 'a combination' (the earlier verdict was behind, not Ready). Times come from the runner's clock and the judge's records: detection runs from the first landing until the runner saw the failure on the combined code (it polls every 10 s); resolution from the fix's push to its Ready verdict. The basket-shape fix, and control-basket-shape's A, were then held at release by the rollback rehearsal (the previous version can't read the new basket shape): the release check, not the combination.

The file's shape, one entry per case id:

```json
{ "date": "2026-10-14", "judge": "<Worker version, commit>", "setup": "<how the projects were run>", "notes": "<anything a reader needs>",
  "cases": { "vat-on-list-price": { "outcome": "<what happened, one line>", "reapplied": "clean | conflict, repaired | conflict, handed back",
    "repair": "<what the repair model did, text-conflict cases only>", "detected": true, "delivered": false, "accepted": false,
    "resolved": true, "interventions": 1, "detectSeconds": 70, "resolveSeconds": 95, "records": ["https://…/verdict"] } } }
```

`detected`: the combined code was rejected; `delivered`: a broken combination became canon or reached production; `accepted` (controls): both changes landed; `repair`: what the judge's repair model made of a text conflict, and whether every fact held on it; `resolved`: a candidate with both changes reached Ready; `interventions`: the actions an agent or a person took to get there.

## What this does not show

- These are 11 designed cases, seeded by Canon's author with known answers, on a small app: evidence that each failure class is caught (and each control accepted) by checks on the combined code, not a measure of how often such conflicts occur or of any system's rate on real work.
- The local queue is a model with the same checks by construction. Its detection is not an advantage or a disadvantage of Canon; the difference to look for is in who re-applies and repairs, what a person has to do, and the time it takes, which only the deployed run measures.
- The seeded repair (`git merge -X theirs`) stands in for a hurried resolution. It is not Canon's repair model, which may keep both sides.
- One run, fixed seeds. Canon's own facts draw new inputs after every push; `vat-is-a-quarter` samples five quantities from 1 to 20, so on the deployed judge it may or may not draw a discounted quantity in the cases where that matters.
